items.claim: The single-verse boundary at Prov.20.17 is correctly warranted and the row properly neutralizes the strongest rival, a same-consonant homograph with the preceding verse.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.20.17 opens עָרֵ֣ב (predicate adjective 'sweet') and closes חָצָֽץ ('gravel'), a self-contained couplet on its own bytes. The row correctly distinguishes עָרֵ֣ב from כִּי in the immediately preceding oshb:Prov.20.16 -- the same three root consonants, but a pointing split (adjective 'sweet' vs. verb 'stood surety'), so a genuine homograph rather than a shared lexeme; no cross-seam catchword survives. Forward neighbor oshb:Prov.20.18 (מַ֭חֲשָׁבוֹת בְּעֵצָ֣ה...) shares no content token with 20:17.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative for Prov.20.23 dismisses the forward rival without disclosing that the shared divine name is part of a three-verse Yahweh run, and never weighs the backward neighbor at all.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.20.22 (לַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה), oshb:Prov.20.23 (יְ֭הוָה), and oshb:Prov.20.24 (מֵיהוָ֥ה) each carry the divine-name token (prov_device_inventory.json yhwh_density.by_chapter['20']=4). The row's rejected_alternative addresses only the forward neighbor ('commerce vocabulary...does not carry into the next verse') without naming that oshb:Prov.20.24 shares the divine-name token with 20:23, and never weighs the backward neighbor oshb:Prov.20.22, which carries the same token into the seam from the other side. The atomic call is still the best-supported reading -- no shared content vocabulary beyond the divine name survives, and the name recurs too densely book-wide (70 verses total) to argue cohesion on its own -- but the cross-seam device is left undisclosed rather than named-and-dismissed, which the standing cross-seam-cohesion rule requires.

items.claim: The single-verse boundary at Prov.20.30 is correctly warranted, its ketiv/qere disclosure is accurate, and no undisclosed neighbor cohesion exists.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.20.30 opens חַבֻּר֣וֹת and closes חַדְרֵי בָֽטֶן, a self-contained synonymous couplet. The verse carries an inline ketiv (תמריק) before the qere (תַּמְר֣וּק), matching pmarks_Prov.json kq['Prov.20.30']=1, and the row discloses it correctly as single-witness. Backward neighbor oshb:Prov.20.29 (תִּפְאֶ֣רֶת בַּחוּרִ֣ים...) and forward neighbor oshb:Prov.21.1 (פַּלְגֵי מַ֣יִם...) share no content token with 20:30.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative for Prov.21.1 names the shared divine name with 21:2 but omits the stronger, more specific shared root and cites no digit for its frequency dismissal.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.21.1 (לֶב מֶ֭לֶךְ ... יְהוָ֑ה) and oshb:Prov.21.2 (closing לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה) share TWO content tokens, not one: the divine name AND the heart root -- 21:1's לֶב מֶ֭לֶךְ (singular, king's heart) and 21:2's לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה (plural construct, hearts weighed by Yahweh). This is the single adjacent pair the device inventory itself flags for the chapter (prov_device_inventory.json catchword_adjacency.shared_pairs_by_chapter['21']=1). The row's rejected_alternative dismisses the pairing solely via an ungrounded frequency claim ('recurs so often...it cannot serve as a cohesion marker') without citing yhwh_density (ch.20=4, ch.21=3 per the inventory) and without naming the heart-root overlap at all. This does not overturn the atomic call -- heart+Yahweh is thematic wisdom-lit vocabulary, not a repeated construction or phrase, and each verse remains a complete image on its own bytes -- but the rival dismissal fails the house discipline requiring a digit-bearing sweep citation for frequency claims and fails to name the full set of shared tokens.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative for Prov.21.2 names the shared divine name with 21:1 but, like the sibling row, omits the shared heart-root token and cites no digit for its frequency dismissal.
items.evidence: Same pair as Prov.21.1: oshb:Prov.21.2 closes לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה, sharing both the divine name and the heart root with oshb:Prov.21.1's לֶב מֶ֭לֶךְ ... יְהוָ֑ה -- the sole flagged catchword-adjacent pair for ch.21 (prov_device_inventory.json catchword_adjacency.shared_pairs_by_chapter['21']=1). The row's rejected_alternative ('that name recurs too widely through the surrounding sayings') again omits the heart-root overlap and lacks the mandated digit-bearing sweep citation (yhwh_density ch.20=4, ch.21=3). The atomic call still holds -- 21:2 closes as a complete antithetic couplet on its own -- but the rival is under-evidenced exactly as in the sibling row P09-031, and the matching omission across both rows points to a systematic gap rather than an isolated slip.
